required_actions: provide a SEPA direct debit mandate
fields.summary_plain_english: The letter asks you to pay the broadcasting fee of 55.08 euros for your apartment for the period October to December 2026. You must transfer the money by 15 November 2026 or you can give a SEPA direct debit mandate.

rows.answer:
The ARD ZDF Deutschlandradio Beitragsservice sends real letters when a broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) is due for a household. A genuine notice will contain your personal contribution number and will ask you to pay the amount (for example 55.08 €) by the stated deadline or to set up a SEPA direct‑debit mandate, which is the safest way to pay [1][3].

If the letter looks like the recent fraud letters – it asks for payment within only a few days, shows a wrong contribution number, uses a different bank account or names the recipient "Radio funk" – it is a fake and the Beitragsservice never sent such a document [1].

A real request is usually sent after the nationwide data‑match (Meldedatenabgleich) when the service discovers a household that has not yet paid the fee. The letter will ask you to confirm your address or to tell the service that someone else already pays the fee for the shared flat; then your data are deleted [3].

In short, a legitimate letter means you have to pay the broadcasting fee for the period mentioned, either by bank transfer or by giving a SEPA mandate. If you suspect fraud, do not transfer money and check the contribution number on the official Beitragsservice website or contact them directly.

required_actions: pay the total amount of 118.16 EUR by 01‑12‑2026
file an objection within one month of receipt if desired
fields.summary_plain_english: You owe 118.16 EUR for the period April to September 2026. The amount must be transferred by 1 December 2026. You may object to this notice within one month after receiving it.

rows.answer: A Festsetzungsbescheid is an official notice that tells you how much Rundfunkbeitrag (broadcasting fee) you have to pay for a certain period. The amount is set according to the Rundfunkbeitragsstaatsvertrag (the broadcasting fee treaty) that all 16 states have approved [3][1]. If you think the amount is wrong, you can file a Widerspruch (objection) within one month after you receive the notice. The one‑month deadline starts when the notice is sent to you, and according to the state law a letter is considered received on the fourth day after it was posted [2]. If you do not object in time, the decision becomes final and cannot be challenged any more [2].

required_actions: inform whether someone already pays the broadcasting fee and provide the contribution number
register the dwelling if no one pays
fields.summary_plain_english: The broadcasting fee office says they cannot match your address to a fee account. They ask you to tell them by 3 December 2026 whether someone already pays the fee for your apartment (and give the contribution number) or to register the apartment yourself.

rows.answer: The letter is part of the nationwide data‑match (Meldedatenabgleich) that the Beitragsservice will carry out in late 2026 [1][2][4]. The service compares the registration data from the local registration offices with its own records to find apartments for which no broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) is yet paid [2][4]. If the match shows a fully‑aged person living at your address who is not yet linked to a fee account, the service sends a letter asking for clarification [2][4]. You must either tell them that another person already pays the fee for the flat and give that person’s nine‑digit contribution number, or you must register the flat yourself [1][3]. If you register, you have to state the move‑in date; the fee will be calculated from that date and may have to be paid retroactively [1]. The first letters are expected to be sent around 14 December 2026, and you have until the deadline (3 December 2026 in your case) to reply [1][2]. If you have a right to exemption or reduction (for example because you receive BAföG or other social benefits), you can claim it retroactively for up to three years, based on the move‑in date and when the exemption criteria were met [1][5].
